title: Project Content — master field definition
x-purpose: THE canonical list of every field we want to capture for a project.
The SOURCE of a field differs per project (one builder ships a designer PDF,
another a price-list photo, another only a portal listing). WHAT we capture
does not. This file is that invariant; extraction scripts are the variable.
Adding a new field is a change to THIS FILE FIRST, then to the Java model,
then to the frontend section registry. Never the other way round.
x-consumers: real_estate_backend                      — Spring Data model + request validation
real_estate_frontend                     — section registry keys off the same paths

importance.required: Page cannot publish without it. Blocks `published: true`.
importance.recommended: Publishable without it, but the project looks thin. Chase it.
importance.optional: Nice to have; many projects will never have it.

sources.rera: UP-RERA portal — already scraped into the `projects` collection. Do NOT hand-extract.
sources.brochure: Builder brochure PDF (often image-only, no text layer)
sources.floor_plan_page: A per-unit floor-plan page inside the brochure
sources.master_plan_page: The site/master plan page inside the brochure
sources.price_list: Builder price list (PDF, photo, or WhatsApp image)
sources.portal: 99acres / Housing / MagicBricks listing — date-label it, never mix with builder figures
sources.builder_direct: Sales team, channel partner, or site visit
sources.derived: Computed by us from other fields — must set provenance.computed = true

x-changelog.note: Initial master definition, derived from the ACE Mahagun Medalleo brochure + price list.
media_ref gains width/height. The frontend needs intrinsic dimensions to reserve layout space before an image loads; without them every floor plan causes layout shift.

clubs[] gains an optional media array (media_ref[]). Added for the Project Showcase redesign, which shows a clubhouse card with a real photo — previously there was no structural way to say which gallery photo belongs to which club, so a component could only guess from captions.

media_ref.asset_id removed (never adopted — GridFS-backed image storage was designed but not built). url is now required and its meaning changed: an object storage key resolved into an absolute CDN URL by real_estate_backend at read time, not a served-app path. Moving derived imagery and RERA document PDFs off local disk / Mongo GridFS onto Cloudflare R2 + a custom CDN domain.

registration_no.description: UP-RERA registration number. Joins this document to the `projects` (RERA) collection.
registration_no.x-extraction: Printed on the brochure back page and every builder creative by law. Must already exist in the projects collection.

slug.description: URL slug. Stable once published — it is a permalink.

published.description: Human gate. The API only serves content where this is true.

display_name.description: Name as marketed, which often differs from the RERA name.
display_name.x-extraction: Brochure cover. RERA says 'Mahagun Medalleo'; the market says 'ACE Mahagun Medalleo'.

tagline.x-extraction: Cover or first spread, e.g. '3 & 4 BHK Luxury Residences & Penthouses'.

locality.description: Sector / colony. The primary SEO term after the project name.

possession_on.description: YYYY-MM. Cross-check against the RERA declared_completion_date and flag divergence.
possession_on.x-extraction: RERA is authoritative; portals are often optimistic. Where they differ, store RERA and note the portal figure.

highlights.description: Short scannable USPs for the hero.

rera_name_differs.description: True when display_name != the RERA project_name, so the UI can show both.

land_area.x-extraction: Brochure master-plan page or portal header. Verify against the RERA land details.

total_units.x-extraction: RERA plan_details row count is authoritative; portals round.

open_area_percent.x-extraction: Only use when the sanctioned denominator is known — never derive it from a green-area sum alone.

green_breakup.x-extraction: Some brochures print a named green-area table per zone. Sum it, but mark the sum computed.

area_basis.description: Which area every price on this project is quoted against.
area_basis.x-extraction: NEVER default this. A rate without a basis is meaningless and legally risky — portals disagree on the same project purely because they mix super and carpet. If the source does not state it, leave the whole pricing block out.

bsp.x-extraction: Header of the price list, e.g. '₹20,995 / sq.ft. W.E.F. 12.04.2026'. Capture the effective date — price lists are reissued.

starting_price.x-extraction: The marketing '₹5.25 Cr*' figure. Keep the display string verbatim, including the asterisk.

payment_plan.x-extraction: The creative headline ('25:25:25:25') and the price list's actual milestones often DIFFER. Capture both — headline in `headline`, the real schedule in `milestones`.

charges.x-extraction: Car parking, club membership, PLC (park-facing / corner), lease rent, IFMS, power backup. Capture the basis — a ₹300 PLC is per-sq.ft., a ₹6,95,000 parking charge is lump sum.

unit_types.description: One entry per distinct saleable configuration. THE core section — everything else is context.
x-extraction: Expect a near-1:1 map between brochure floor-plan pages and price-list size rows; a mismatch means a missing plan or a discontinued config.
Builders name plans by TOWER FAMILY, not by BHK ('Gold/Platinum Palace - 3 BHK'). Capture the family — it is what links a unit to a wing on the master plan.
Cross-check every super area against the price list. Transposed SQ.M./SQ.FT. columns and stale sizes are common; see the balcony row on Medalleo p.24.

key.description: Stable slug; the tab id and URL hash. Never change once published.

variant.description: 'Type I' / 'Unit 2' — disambiguates same-BHK plans in one family.

config_label.description: Verbatim from the price list, e.g. '4 BHK + Servant + FL + PR'.

extras.description: Parsed from config_label. Stored as an enum array so it is filterable across projects.
extras.x-extraction: FL = Family Lounge, PR = Powder Room, S = Servant. Expand the abbreviations.

wings.description: Wing/tower numbers this plan applies to. Powers the clickable master plan.
wings.x-extraction: The 'WING NO. 28, 31, 32 & 35' header above the area table.

is_full_floor.x-extraction: True when the plan page shows a whole floor plate as one apartment.

areas.description: Store BOTH units exactly as printed. Do not convert — divergence between sources is signal, not noise.
areas.x-extraction: The 4-row area table on each plan page: SUPER / BUILT UP / CARPET / BALCONY, in SQ.M. and SQ.FT. columns. Sanity-check: carpet < built_up < super, and balcony sq.m. must be far smaller than the flat's sq.m.

price.x-extraction: indicative_total = bsp_per_sqft × areas.super.sqft. Always set computed: true — it is not a builder quote.

plan_2d.x-extraction: Crop the plan artwork off the page and store the normalized bbox in ProjectAsset.origin so the crop is reproducible.

plan_3d.x-extraction: NOT present in brochures — brochures carry 2D plans only. Produced separately (isometric render commissioned from the 2D plan). Never a publishing gate.

amenities.description: Grouped, never one flat list — grouping is what makes 40 amenities readable.
amenities.x-extraction: Brochure amenity spreads. Keep the builder's own grouping (Landscape / Clubhouse / Terrace) and record access restrictions.

clubs.x-extraction: Where a project has tiered clubs, capture the access rule explicitly — 'owner-only' must never be flattened into a generic amenity.

media.description: Photo(s) of this specific club. Optional — many gallery photos exist per project but none are structurally tied to a club without this; do not guess the link from a caption match, leave it empty instead.

connectivity.description: Distance/time to landmarks. High-value SEO content.
connectivity.x-extraction: The brochure's connectivity spread. Builder minutes are optimistic — prefer distance_km where both are given.

specifications.x-extraction: Usually a dense table on the second-to-last brochure page. Often absent from designer brochures — then ask the builder.

master_plan.x-extraction: The site-plan page. Worth extra care — wing numbers on it link to unit_types[].wings.

custom_sections.description: Escape hatch for the per-builder long tail. Rendered by primitive renderers — needs no schema change and no frontend code.
custom_sections.x-extraction: Use for one-off blocks ('Vastu Compliance', 'NRI Corner'). If the same custom section shows up on three projects, promote it to a real field in this file.

section_order.description: Per-project override of the default section order.

hidden_sections.description: Section ids to suppress for this project.

sources.description: The traceability register. Every contested fact points at one of these.
sources.x-extraction: One entry per document/portal actually used, with the date it was valid. This is what lets the page say 'Possession: Sep 2029 (portal data, Aug 2026)' instead of asserting it.

url.description: Either an external citation URL (e.g. a portal listing) or, if the source itself was uploaded, a bare object storage key resolved the same way as media_ref.url.

measure.description: Any physical quantity. Never store a bare number, never store '10 acres' as a string.

area_pair.description: Both units, exactly as printed on the source sheet.

media_ref.description: url is an object storage key relative to the CDN bucket (e.g. 'media/UPRERAPRJ125561/exterior-hero.webp'), not a domain. The API composes it into an absolute CDN URL at read time (app.cdn-base-url in real_estate_backend) so switching storage providers later never requires rewriting stored content. A value already starting with 'http://' or 'https://' is treated as an external asset and passed through unchanged.

alt.description: Required for SEO and a11y on every public image.

width.description: Intrinsic pixel width. Required by the frontend image pipeline to reserve space before load — omitting it causes cumulative layout shift, which is a ranking signal.

provenance.description: Attach to any fact that can be contested across sources.

note.description: Rendered on the page when confidence is not high.
